<Callout type="warn" title="Design in progress">
  This format is being designed and **is not implemented**. Nothing on this page is a stable
  syntax. To ship a plugin today, write a [remote plugin](/docs/build/remote-plugin) (MCP) or a
  [bundled plugin](/docs/build/bundled-plugin) (SDK).
</Callout>

## Why

Today a plugin is either code that ships inside the app (bundled, needs an app release) or a
server someone has to run (remote MCP). Many campus integrations are simpler than that: a few
authenticated requests to a campus service, some extraction, and a card to show the result. The
declarative format aims to make those as easy to share as an agent skill: a folder, or a link to
one.

## The direction

As currently planned (subject to change):

| Part | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `PLUGIN.md` | The manifest and the instructions for the agent |
| `tools/*.yaml` | Tools described as data: campus requests, then extraction and transformation of the response |
| `ui/*.json` | [Generative-UI](/docs/concepts/generative-ui) specs for cards, forms and widgets |

- **The app interprets it.** No compiled code is downloaded, so a new plugin or an update needs no
  app release.
- **Install by pasting a link.**
- The rules that apply to every plugin stay: typed tools with honest effects, permissions and
  consent, campus requests made by the harness (credentials never leave the device), and tool
  results treated as data.

## The spec

The specification is written in the app repository:
[`docs/PLUGIN-LANGUAGE.md`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness/blob/master/docs/PLUGIN-LANGUAGE.md).
It may not be published yet; follow [`pkuinfo/pku-harness`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness)
for progress. These docs will document the format once it is implemented.

## What to do meanwhile

- Design your tools as you would for any plugin ([Tools and schemas](/docs/build/tools)): small,
  one effect each, data-only results. That design carries over.
- Port the protocol from [pkucli](/docs/build/porting-from-pkucli) and keep notes of the exact
  requests and the fields you extract: that is what a declarative tool will describe.
- Ship it now as a remote plugin if it doesn't need the user's campus session.
